{{ill|Takachiho-gawara|en|Takachiho-gawara|qid=Q10566710|lt=Takachiho-gawara}} the location of the descent from heaven is present on the shrine grounds.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Kirishima Guide {{!}} JapanVisitor Japan Travel Guide |url=https://www.japanvisitor.com/japan-city-guides/kirishima-guide |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.japanvisitor.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="env.go.jp">{{Cite web |title=Ministry of the Environment_Let’s visit the National Parks of Japan!_Kirishima_Recommended course_Kirishima Mythology Course |url=https://www.env.go.jp/en/nature/nps/park/guide/kirishima/recommend/09.html |access-date=2018-11-16 |website=www.env.go.jp |language=en}}</ref>

Historically, the entire of {{ill|Mount Kirishima|en|Mount Kirishima|qid=Q1319361|lt=Mount Kirishima}} is considered part of the shrine grounds. Today, parts of the mountains where festivals take place and the location of the [[Tenson kōrin]] is considered part of the shrine grounds.

It is dedicated to [[Konohanasakuya-hime]], [[Hoori]], {{ill|Toyotama-hime|de|Toyotama-hime|es|Toyotama-hime|fa|تویوتاما-هیمه|fi|Otohime|fr|Otohime|id|Toyotama-hime|ja|トヨタマヒメ|ko|도요타마히메|mni|ꯇꯣꯌꯣꯇꯃ-ꯍꯤꯃꯦ|pl|Toyotama-hime|ru|Тоётама-химэ|simple|Toyotama-hime|sv|Otohime|uk|Тойотама-хіме|vi|Toyotama-hime|zh|豐玉毘賣命|qid=Q2329261|lt=Toyotama-hime}}, [[Ugayafukiaezu]], [[Tamayori-hime (mother of Jimmu)|Tamayori-bime]] and [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto]]. This shrine holds several {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|de|Wichtiges Kulturgut Japans|es|Bien Cultural Importante de Japón|fi|Japanin tärkeä kulttuuriomaisuus|fr|Bien culturel important|id|Properti Kebudayaan Penting (Jepang)|it|Bene culturale importante (Giappone)|ja|重要文化財|ko|일본의 중요문화재|ro|Patrimoniu cultural important al Japoniei|simple|Important Cultural Properties of Japan|th|ทรัพย์สินทางวัฒนธรรมที่สำคัญ (ญี่ปุ่น)|tr|Önemli Kültürel Varlık (Japonya)|uk|Важливі культурні пам'ятки Японії|zh|重要文化財|qid=Q1188622|lt=Important Cultural Properties}}, such as the ''[[honden]]'', ''[[Heiden (Shinto)|heiden]]'', ''[[Haiden (Shinto)|haiden]]'', {{Nihongo||登廊下|tōrōka}}, {{Nihongo||勅使殿|Chōkushiden}} etc. It has been destroyed several times by [[:en:Volcanic|Volcanic]] [[:en:Eruption|Eruption]]s.

== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines the following seven deities:<ref>[http://www.kirishimajingu.or.jp/contents/goyuisho.html Official website]</ref>
; Main deity
:* [[Ninigi-no-Mikoto|Ama-no-sakahoko no mikoto]]
; Deities enshrined together

== History ==
[[File:Takachiho-gawara Kirishima City Kagoshima Pref02n4050.jpg|right|thumb|Ruins of the old shrine]]
[[File:Kirishima-jingu15n4350.jpg|thumb|150px|Sacred cedar tree]]
According to legend, during the reign of Emperor Kinmei (6th century), a monk named Keiin built a shrine between [[Mount Takachiho]] and the crater {{ill|Otake|de|Ōtake (Begriffsklärung)|fr|Otake|id|Otake|it|Ōtake (disambigua)|ko|오타케|nds|Ōtake|ru|Отакэ|uk|Отаке (значення)|qid=Q7108397|lt=Otake}}, known as Setao (Setao or Seta Ridge).<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|title=Kagoshima Prefecture Encyclopedia |date=March 8, 1983 |publisher=Kadokawa Shoten}}</ref> Some sources suggest the shrine was established in the first year of Emperor Kinmei's reign (540).<ref>{{Cite book|title=Hometown Shrine: Kagoshima Prefecture Shrine Gazette |date=April 30, 1995 |publisher=Kagoshima Prefecture Shinto Youth Association}}</ref>

Mount Takachiho is believed to be the site of the legendary descent of the gods ([[:en:Tenson Korin|Tenson Korin]]), and the shrine originally began as a form of mountain worship.<ref></ref>

The original location of the shrine was close to the crater, and the shrine buildings were frequently destroyed by eruptions. The shrine was rebuilt in Setao in {{ill|940|en|940|qid=Q23830|lt=940}} or {{ill|950|ab|950|af|950|am|950 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|950|ar|950|ary|950|arz|950|ast|950|avk|950|az|950|azb|۹۵۰ (میلادی)|ban|950|bar|950|bcl|950|be|950|be_x_old|950|bg|950|bn|৯৫০|bpy|মারি ৯৫০|br|950|bs|950.|ca|950|cdo|950 nièng|ceb|950|ckb|٩٥٠|crh|950|cs|950|csb|950|cv|950|cy|950|da|950|de|950|el|950|eml|950|eo|950|es|950|et|950|eu|950|fa|۹۵۰ (میلادی)|fi|950|fo|950|fr|950|fy|950|ga|950|gan|950年|gd|950|gl|950|he|950|hi|950|hr|950.|ht|950 (almanak jilyen)|hu|950|hy|950|id|950|ilo|950|io|950|is|950|it|950|ja|950年|jv|950|ka|950|kaa|950|kk|950 жыл|ko|950년|la|950|lb|950|lij|950|lmo|950|lt|950 m.|lv|950. gads|map_bms|950|mdf|950|mg|950|mhr|950|mi|950|mk|950|mr|इ.स. ९५०|mrj|950 и|ms|950|mzn|۹۵۰|nah|950|nap|950|nds|950|new|सन् ९५०|nl|950|nn|950|no|950|nrm|950|nso|950|oc|950|or|୯୫୦|os|950-æм аз|pl|950|pnb|950|pt|950|qu|950|ro|950|ru|950 год|rue|950|sa|९५०|scn|950|sd|950ع|se|950|sh|950.|shn|950|si|950|simple|950|sk|950|sl|950|smn|950|sq|950|sr|950|su|950|sv|950|sw|950|tg|Соли 950|th|พ.ศ. 1493|tk|950|tl|950|tly|950|tr|950|tt|950 ел|uk|950|ur|950ء|uz|950|vec|950|vi|950|vls|950|war|950|wuu|950年|xmf|950|zea|950|zh|950年|zh_min_nan|950 nî|zh_yue|950年|qid=Q23449|lt=950}} by the monk Shokuu, but it continued to be affected by eruptions.<ref name=":0" />

nî|zh_yue|1715年|qid=Q6884|lt=1715}} by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]].<ref name=":0" />

Historically, the shrine was also known as the "West Shrine" and was one of two shrines, the other being the "East Shrine" (now [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]]).<ref>{{Cite book|title=Shrine Encyclopedia |date=September 25, 1997 |publisher=Tokyo-do Publishing}}</ref> Another theory suggests that the shrine was divided into [[Kirishima Zuka Shrine]] and [[Higashi Kirishima Shrine]], with the current Kirishima Jingu being derived from the West Shrine.<ref></ref>

The Shimazu clan worshipped at the shrine, and Shimazu Yoshihisa drew lots there before the {{ill|Battle of Mimigawa|fa|نبرد میمیگاوا|fr|Bataille de la Mimi-gawa|it|Battaglia di Mimigawa|ja|耳川の戦い|ko|미미가와 전투|sr|Битка код Мимигаве|zh|耳川之戰|qid=Q4871739|lt=Battle of Mimigawa}} in 1578. The shrine was also consulted on important decisions during the clan's campaigns.<ref></ref>

[[:en:Sakamoto Ryoma|Sakamoto Ryoma]] visited the shrine during his honeymoon trip to the Kirishima mountain range, where the sacred "Heavenly Reverse Spear" is believed to have been planted by the deity Ama-no-sakahoko.<ref>Sakamoto Ryoma{{Aozora Bunko|000908|51734|Shinji Kyukana|Letter to Otome on December 4, 1866}}</ref>

Before the Meiji period's [[Shinbutsu bunri]] (separation of Shinto and Buddhism) decree, the shrine was known as "West Shrine Kirishima Gongen" and had an Eleven-faced Kannon as its main deity. It was also a central site for the [[Kirishima Rokushagu Shrine]] worship by Shugendo practitioners.<ref></ref> In 1874, it was designated as a Kanpei-taisha under the modern shrine Ranking system.

On November 16, 1935, Emperor Showa visited the shrine after the conclusion of the Imperial Army's special exercises.<ref>{{Cite book|author=Hara Takeshi |title=Showa Emperor's Special Train Records |publisher=Shinchosha |date=September 30, 2016 |page=77|isbn=978-4-10-320523-4}}</ref>

The sacred cedar tree at the shrine is estimated to be about 800 years old and is considered the ancestor of southern Kyushu's cedar trees.<ref></ref>

== festivals ==
Approximately 100 festivals are held annually at Kirishima Jingu.
* Tsuitachi-sai (Monthly festival) - 1st of every month
* Tsukinami-sai - 19th of every month
* Saitan-sai - January 1
* Hatsuniku-sai - January 2
* Genshi-sai - January 3
* Uchimaki-sai - February 18 (Old Lunar New Year)
* Otaue-sai - March 3 (Old Lunisolar February 4)
* Sanada no Osada Otaue-sai - First Sunday of June
* Oharae-shiki - June 30, December 31
* Southern Kyushu Kagura - Last Saturday of August
* festival - September 19
* Joyasai - December 31

== Cultural Properties ==
=== National Treasures ===
* Main Shrine, Heiden, Haiden (with two roof plaques) - Designated on February 9, 2022<ref>Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Notice No. 9, February 9, 2022.</ref>.

=== Important Cultural Properties ===
* Nabori-roka (Climbing Corridor)
* Chokushiden
(In addition, the following are designated as "attached" properties)
* Gates Guard Shrine (2 buildings)
* Shrine Banquet Hall (1 building)
<gallery>
File:Kirishima-jingu03n4592.jpg|Chokushiden (side view)
File:Kirishima-jingu05n4440.jpg|Haiden
File:Kirishima-jingu06n4592.jpg|Climbing Corridor
</gallery>
These shrine buildings were donated by [[Shimazu Yoshitaka]] and constructed in 1715. The buildings are brightly painted and elaborately decorated. The main shrine is particularly luxurious, with red lacquered pillars, beams, and railings adorned with colorful patterns and gilded metal fittings, while the walls are covered with vividly painted relief panels. Such ornate decoration in both exterior and interior is rare in shrine architecture, earning it the nickname "Nikko of the West."

== Precincts ==
The entire area around Mount Kirishima was originally the shrine's precincts, but during the {{ill|Abolition of the han system|ca|Abolició del sistema han|de|Abschaffung der Han|es|Abolición del sistema han|fa|لغو سیستم هان|fr|Abolition du système han|he|ביטול שיטת ההאן|id|Penghapusan sistem domain|it|Abolizione del sistema han|ja|廃藩置県|ko|폐번치현|lt|Han sistemos panaikinimas|ms|Pemansuhan sistem han|pl|Haihan-chiken|pt|Abolição do sistema han|ru|Ликвидация ханов и основание префектур|th|การยกเลิกระบบแคว้น|tr|Han sisteminin kaldırılması|uk|Ліквідація ханів і заснування префектур|vi|Phế phiên, lập huyện|wuu|废藩置县|zh|廢藩置縣|zh_classical|廢藩置縣|zh_min_nan|Hòe-phoan-tì-koān|zh_yue|廢藩置縣|qid=Q331905|lt=Abolition of the han system}} in 1871, the boundary of the precincts was redrawn to follow the summit of Mount Kirishima, excluding the Miyazaki Prefecture side. In 1882, 7810 hectares were further reduced, and with the establishment of the {{ill|Constitution of Japan|ar|دستور اليابان|as|জাপানৰ সংবিধান|az|Yaponiya konstitusiyası|be|Канстытуцыя Японіі|bxr|Японой Үндэһэн Хуули|ca|Constitució del Japó|ckb|دەستووری ژاپۆن|de|Verfassung des Staates Japan|el|Σύνταγμα της Ιαπωνίας|eo|Konstitucio de Japanio|es|Constitución de Japón|et|Jaapani põhiseadus|fa|قانون اساسی ژاپن|fi|Japanin perustuslaki|fr|Constitution du Japon|he|חוקת יפן|hi|जापान का संविधान|hu|Japán alkotmánya|hy|Ճապոնիայի սահմանադրություն|id|Konstitusi Jepang|it|Costituzione del Giappone|ja|日本国憲法|ka|იაპონიის კონსტიტუცია|ko|일본국 헌법|la|Constitutio Iaponiae|lt|Japonijos Konstitucija|lv|Japānas Konstitūcija|mn|Японы Үндсэн Хууль|ms|Perlembagaan Jepun|ne|जापानको संविधान|nl|Japanse Grondwet|no|Japans grunnlov|pl|Konstytucja Japonii|pnb|جاپان دا آئین|pt|Constituição do Japão|ro|Constituția Japoniei|ru|Конституция Японии|simple|Constitution of Japan|sv|Japans konstitution|th|รัฐธรรมนูญแห่งญี่ปุ่น|tl|Saligang Batas ng Hapon|tr|Japonya Anayasası|uk|Конституція Японії|ur|آئین جاپان|vi|Hiến pháp Nhật Bản|zh|日本国宪法|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún-kok Hiàn-hoat|qid=Q237082|lt=Constitution of Japan}} in 1946, most of the shrine's forests became national land. Subsequently, 789 hectares necessary for shrine ceremonies were returned to the shrine.<ref>Editorial Committee of Kirishima Town History, 'Kirishima Town History', Kirishima Town, 1992.</ref>
